page.filesDescription: The raw files of this measurement. They are never changed.
page.analysisDescription: Compute values from the files and send them to this sample's result columns.
page.noFiles: No files attached yet. Use the paperclip to attach the files of this measurement.

chooser.title: What kind of measurement is this?
chooser.description: The analysis is chosen from the technique name. Pick one if the name does not say.

edx.spotsDescription: Untick a spot to leave it out of the averages. Its files are never changed.
edx.noSpots: No quantification.csv found. Attach the sample's folder, the export folder from the microscope, with the paperclip.
edx.allExcluded: Every spot is left out. Tick at least one.
edx.problems: These files could not be read:

reasons.missingColumns: missing the Element symbol or Atomic concentration columns
reasons.invalidNumber: a concentration is not a number
reasons.unreadable: the file could not be read

edx.noSpectra: No spectrum.emsa found next to the quantification files.

ellipsometry.noFile: Attach the fit export, a .csv such as AAA159_seqfit.csv, with the paperclip.
ellipsometry.unreadable: This CSV is not a fit export, or a number in its summary is missing.
ellipsometry.notice: These are the Average and StdDeviation rows of the file, as the instrument software wrote them.

results.title: Send to results
results.description: Tick the values to put in this sample's result columns. Nothing is saved until you press the button.
results.apply: Send {count, plural, one {# value} other {# values}} to results
results.applied: {count, plural, one {# value} other {# values}} sent to the results
results.failed: The values could not be sent. Check the columns and names.
results.columnTaken: Each result column can only receive one value.
results.nameMissing: Give each new column a name.

workspace.description: Analyse raw files from the instrument, or the samples of an experiment.

upload.edxDescription: Drop a sample's folder from the microscope, or several. Nothing is uploaded or saved: the files are read in your browser.
upload.ellipsometryDescription: Drop one or more fit exports (.csv). Nothing is uploaded or saved: the files are read in your browser.
upload.dropHint: quantification.csv and spectrum.emsa are read; the other files are ignored
upload.levelDate: A folder holding several samples (a date folder)
upload.noFiles: No quantification.csv was found in what you dropped.
upload.noCsv: No .csv file was found in what you dropped.
upload.problems: These files could not be read:

reasons.invalidNumber: a number in the summary is missing

upload.ftirDescription: Drop one or more FTIR exports (.csv or .txt). Nothing is uploaded or saved: the files are read in your browser.
upload.dropHintFtir: Two columns: wavenumber and value, with or without a header
upload.noFtirFiles: No readable spectrum was found in what you dropped.

experiment.pickHint: Choose a project and an experiment to analyse its samples.
experiment.noExperiments: This project has no experiments yet.
experiment.noRows: This experiment has no {technique} measurements yet. Record one on a sample and attach its files.
experiment.valuesDescription: Choose once what goes to the result columns. It applies to every sample you tick.
experiment.rowsDescription: Tick the samples to work on. Open one to leave out bad spots. A sample that would replace a different value is skipped unless you tick Update.
experiment.filesUnreadable: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} could not be read
experiment.apply: Apply to {count, plural, one {# sample} other {# samples}}
experiment.applied: {count, plural, one {# sample} other {# samples}} updated
experiment.failed: The values could not be sent. Check the columns and names.
experiment.pickSamples: Tick at least one sample to update.
experiment.ftirRowsDescription: Tick the samples to compare: their spectra are stacked below, read and processed the same way, with one list of peaks.
experiment.ftirValuesDescription: Choose which peak values go to which result columns. It applies to every sample you tick. A sample with no data near a chosen peak cannot be updated.
experiment.ftirNoPeaks: Keep some peaks first: detect them or click the spectrum.

ftir.noFile: Attach an FTIR export (.csv or .txt) to this characterization to analyse it.
ftir.unreadableTitle: These files could not be read:

reasons.empty: the file is empty or missing
reasons.invalidLine: line {line} is not a wavenumber and a value
reasons.tooFewPoints: it has too few points to be a spectrum

ftir.dropped: {count, plural, one {# point at 0 % or below has} other {# points at 0 % or below have}} no absorbance and {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} left out.

guess.percentTransmittance: The values run up to about 100 and stay high, like percent transmittance.
guess.absorbanceRange: The values are small, like absorbance.
guess.ambiguous: The values are between 0 and 1: they could be absorbance or a transmittance fraction. Choose the right one.
guess.unclear: The values fit neither well. Choose what they are.

controls.convertHint: A = 2 − log10(%T). Absorbance is the scale that follows Beer–Lambert, so peak heights compare better. For a thin film on a substrate, interference can still distort absolute values.
controls.normaliseNote: Normalised values are relative, not absolute amounts, and the original file is never changed.

problems.flat: This spectrum (or range) is flat, so it cannot be scaled.
problems.noReference: No data was found near the reference peak, so the spectrum is shown unnormalised.
problems.zeroReference: The value at the reference peak is 0, so it cannot be used.

controls.searchHint: Leave empty to look across the whole spectrum.
controls.detectNote: These are suggestions: remove the ones that are noise and add any that were missed. Peaks you have labelled stay as they are.

chart.clickHint: Click the spectrum to add a peak at that wavenumber.

peaks.title: Peaks
peaks.empty: No peaks yet. Detect them, click the spectrum, or add one by its position.

export.convertedLine: Absorbance, converted from percent transmittance (A = 2 − log10 %T)
export.stackedLine: Spectra are shifted vertically to compare them; the vertical axis is not to scale.

bonds.title: Bond table
bonds.description: The bonds you look for, with the wavenumber range you trust and where it comes from. A detected peak offers the bonds whose range it falls in; you decide what to keep. The app has no built-in list.
bonds.empty: No bonds yet. Add the ones you look for, or paste or import a table.
bonds.sourcePlaceholder: A paper, a book, a note
bonds.toHint: Leave empty for a single position (matched within the tolerance).
bonds.deleteDescription: Peaks you already labelled keep their labels.

errors.missingBond: Write what the bond is called.
errors.rangeOrder: From must not be higher than To.
errors.duplicate: This bond and range are already in the table.
errors.alreadyThere: This bond and range are already in the table.
errors.tooMany: The table is full: it holds at most {max} bonds.
errors.failed: The bond could not be saved.

import.title: Paste or import a table
import.format: The first row names the columns: Bond, From (cm-1), To (cm-1) and Source, in any order. Bond and From are required. Leave To empty for a single position. Source is optional. Numbers may use a point or a comma for decimals. Copy rows from Excel and paste them, or import a CSV or Excel file.
import.dropTitle: Or import a CSV or Excel file
import.fileFailed: This file could not be read as a table.
import.ready: {count, plural, one {# bond is} other {# bonds are}} ready to add.
import.problemsTitle: These rows cannot be used and are left out:

problems.noHeader: Row {row}: the first row must name the columns; Bond and From are required.
problems.rangeOrder: Row {row}: From is higher than To.
problems.duplicate: Row {row}: the same bond and range appear twice.
problems.alreadyThere: Row {row}: this bond and range are already in the table.

import.addButton: Add {count, plural, one {# bond} other {# bonds}}
import.replaceButton: Replace the table with {count, plural, one {# bond} other {# bonds}}
import.confirmReplace: This removes the {existing, plural, one {# bond} other {# bonds}} now in the table. Replace it?
import.added: {count, plural, one {# bond} other {# bonds}} added
import.replaced: The table now has {count, plural, one {# bond} other {# bonds}}
import.failed: The table could not be saved. Check that no row repeats one already there.
